title: A Message about the City of Kings Let's Play
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LpqnF4FROjg

Daniel (@dungeondive) posts a brief mea culpa: the City of Kings playthrough is being reset. Waking early and pressing on into Chapter Three before enough coffee, he made so many small errors that the session became, in his words, meaningless — corrections piling on corrections — and he was fairly sure he was about to lose badly to one of the creatures anyway. So he's scrapping it and starting over from Chapter One with the same heroes, incorporating fixes viewers flagged (a shout-out to a commenter named Glen). It's a short, candid clip, and its real value is honesty: he cheerfully promises he'll "probably never play a game a hundred percent correctly," and frames the whole exercise as a way to get better at learning and teaching games on camera. Barely two minutes long, it's the hinge of the City of Kings saga — the moment the ambitious story playthrough quietly collapses and pivots toward a single standalone scenario instead. A small artifact, but an oddly telling one about the difficulty of unedited board-game video and the temperament it demands.

----

Daniel scrapped an entire playthrough rather than post one riddled with errors. When you're learning a game, do you restart to get it right, or push on and fix mistakes as you go?
